correctness.rationale: Four-round EF matching of clone parts proves coordinatewise clipping at four for all positive part sizes. The complete tuple-type recurrence exactly represents formulas at the remaining quantifier rank; quotienting by unused-clone automorphisms preserves every extension orbit. All 1024 four-clipped vectors were exhaustively classified into 33 rank-four signatures and tested equal to their three-clipped vectors. A separately implemented labelled-vertex oracle verified all 243 three-clipped graphs and 29403 pairwise comparisons. Exactly one signature has minimum representative order 15, and its 4-clipped vectors all have five coordinates at least three, proving sharpness in the infinite family.

originality.rationale: The primary literature establishes pentagon blow-ups as natural objects and supplies EF comparisons for unblown paths/cycles, but none of the actually inspected results entails the exact four-round equivalence classes for five independent clone populations. Indexed published results contain neighbouring games and graph-family results but no examined equivalent or stronger statement. Indexed searches produced unrelated constructions or different logical signatures. The claim is specifically the 33-class calculation and the unexpectedly sharp three-clone reduction, not the general game recurrence. Residual historical overlap is acknowledged.
residual_risks: A paper using modular decomposition, independent-set substitution or false-twin expansion terminology rather than pentagon blow-up could contain equivalent coverage.
Indexed retrieval and selected full-text inspections do not prove global novelty.

value.rationale: The C5 independent-clone graphs are a natural five-parameter class used for triangle-free pentagon extremizers. The theorem gives a complete rank-four first-order testing set (33 theories), a nontrivial global collapse to three clones per part, and a genuinely sharp smallest maximum representative size of 15; this characterizes a motivated full logical invariant over infinitely many finite structures, not an arbitrary small enumerated slice.
